blocks.text: The systemic circulation supplies oxygenated blood to all the cells, tissues, and organs of the body (except lungs) and returns deoxygenated blood to heart. It consists of the following components:

The heart walls are supplied with blood through a small portion of the systemic circulation. Two coronary arteries i.e., right and left coronary arteries arise from aorta, near its origin. These arteries divide into many smaller arteries, arterioles and then into capillaries. After supplying oxygenated blood to heart muscles, the capillaries unite to form venules which make many coronary veins. The coronary veins join to form a coronary sinus, which opens in right atrium. Small coronary veins drain directly into right atrium.

blocks.alt: Two views of the heart with the vena cava and aorta above. Anterior view: the left and right coronary arteries arise from the base of the aorta and branch over the heart wall. Posterior view: coronary veins run up into the large coronary sinus that crosses the back of the heart, with the right coronary artery below it. The coronary veins label points to both hearts.
blocks.caption: Figure 11.14: Coronary circulation (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 11.14).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Left coronary artery, Right coronary artery, Coronary veins, Coronary sinus, Right coronary artery, (Anterior view), (Posterior view).

blocks.text: A portal system is a circulation in which veins end in capillaries. In hepatic portal system, a large hepatic portal vein collects blood from spleen and alimentary canal and take it to liver. The blood from liver is taken to heart through hepatic veins.

blocks.alt: The liver with the stomach, spleen and pancreas beside it, and the colon framing the small intestine below. Veins from the small intestine, colon, pancreas and spleen join into the hepatic portal vein, which enters the liver and branches there. Hepatic veins carry blood from the liver into the inferior vena cava, which runs up the middle.
blocks.caption: Figure 11.15: Hepatic portal system (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 11.15).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Inferior vena cava, Hepatic veins, Spleen, Pancreas, Hepatic portal vein, Ascending colon, Descending colon, Small intestine.

blocks.text: The blood that comes from alimentary canal to liver contains substances that are absorbed from small intestine. These substances pass through liver before going to heart. Liver removes harmful substances from blood and absorbs nutrients for storage before sending this blood to heart. Hepatic portal system extends from the lower portion of oesophagus to the upper part of anal canal.

It is another important component of the systemic circulation. Right and left renal arteries carry oxygenated blood to the right and left kidneys. Inside the kidney, each renal artery divides repeatedly to make smaller arteries. The smaller arteries branch into several afferent arterioles, which supply blood to nephrons (units of kidney). Each afferent arteriole divides to make the capillaries of glomeruli.

The capillaries of glomeruli unite to make efferent arteriole, which divides to make two sets of capillaries i.e., (i) peri-tubular capillaries (around nephron tubule in cortical portion of kidney), and (ii) vasa recta (around nephron tubule in the medulla of kidney). These capillaries unite to form venules that converge and make smaller veins. The smaller veins unit to form a renal vein.

blocks.alt: Left: a nephron with its blood supply. A smaller artery gives the afferent arteriole, which forms the glomerulus; the efferent arteriole leaves it and forms peri-tubular capillaries round the coiled tubule and vasa recta along the loop; a venule drains into a smaller vein. Right: a kidney in section with smaller arteries spreading from the renal artery, and the renal vein leaving it.
blocks.caption: Figure 11.16: Renal circulation (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 11.16, printed as 'Renal portal system').
blocks.long_description: Labels: Peri-tubular capillaries, Efferent arteriole, Glomerulus, Afferent arteriole, Smaller arteries, Vasa recta, Venule, Smaller vein, Renal vein, Renal artery.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 11.16 is captioned 'Renal portal system'. Humans have no renal portal system; the figure shows the renal circulation (the book's own heading), so it is captioned 'Renal circulation' above.
